conceptual assets.information: The application or instruction words held in the internal ROM or RAM are the contents returned for instruction-memory reads and, in RAM mode, replaced by bus writes. They enter through bus write data and leave through the bus response data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The memory contents may be confidential application code or data, and ROM/RAM words can be exposed through rdata and bus_rsp_o.data at lines 81, 95, 128-131, 159-162, and 185. The RAM implementation accepts bus_req_i.data into memory words on write accesses at lines 114-126 and 143-155, allowing the contents to be overwritten. Instruction reads depend on these contents and the response data can be withheld by the request-derived rden gate at lines 176 and 185, so loss or withholding can prevent correct instruction transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read application words through the response, overwrite RAM contents with bus writes, or suppress the returned words so instruction fetches fail.

conceptual assets.information: The address selecting an instruction-memory word determines which word a bus access reads or writes. It enters as bus_req_i.addr and has no output port because it only indexes internal storage.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An altered address is used as the memory index at lines 116, 119, 122, 125, 128-131, and 145, 148, 151, 154, so it can redirect a read or write to a different memory word and compromise memory integrity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter bus_req_i.addr so a read or write targets an unintended instruction-memory word.

conceptual assets.information: This internally held decision enables a requested read and controls whether the stored memory word is placed on the response data port. It is derived from the bus request and has no direct entry or exit port because its source fields are access-command fields and it only gates the response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Unauthorized alteration of rden changes whether bus_rsp_o.data is driven through the gate at lines 176 and 185, compromising the integrity of the read response. The same gate can withhold required memory data and prevent instruction fetches from completing at lines 176 and 185.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the request-derived enable to cause an unintended response or suppress memory data and stall instruction fetches.

considered, not kept.reason: bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw, and bus_req_i.ben only describe whether, in which direction, and which bytes of a memory access are used, so Access command fields bars them as pieces of their own.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and error status
considered, not kept.reason: bus_rsp_o.ack is a transaction handshake and bus_rsp_o.err is tied to a constant, so Transfer records and Bus handshake copies provide no independent conceptual asset.
The clock and reset only time, initialize, or release other elements and are excluded as conceptual assets by the Clocks and resets rule.
IMEM_SIZE, IMEM_INIT, and alt_style_c only select the built memory implementation and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
